groups.defect: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in optimized_image.rb. Ruby uses the last definition, so the later (from, to, dimensions, opts) version silently replaces the max_width/max_height version and leaves it as dead code. This breaks callers that use the old signature: the 5-arg call in resize_emoji.rb:14 raises ArgumentError, 4-arg calls raise TypeError or produce bad geometry, and the new controller call only works by accident of last-definition-wins. The fix is to keep a single dimensions-string definition and port old-signature callers to it.

answer.reasoning: All seven suggestions report the same root defect: a second `downsize` definition replaces the width/height one, which leaves dead code and breaks the old calling contract. Both judges agree on this grouping, and the diff confirms it. The only open question is needsUnifiedComment. The members point to different concrete effects. Some cite the resize_emoji.rb:14 5-arg ArgumentError and say to update that caller, which is an edit in a second file. Others cite the 4-arg TypeError, the width-only geometry, or how fragile the uploads_controller call is. No single member covers all of these, so the merged comment has to carry more than any one of them. That makes true the better choice, but you could argue for false because these are all consequences of one defect. That is why decisive is false.
